text:
I

And above all, look with innocence. As if nothing were happening, which is true.


II

But I want to look at you until your face draws away from my fear like a bird from the sharp edge of night.


III

Like a girl drawn in pink chalk on a very old wall, suddenly erased by the rain.


IV

As when a flower opens and reveals the heart it does not have.


V

All the gestures of my body and my voice to make of myself the offering, the bouquet the wind abandons on the threshold.


VI

Cover the memory of your face with the mask of what you will be and frighten the girl you were.


VII

The night of the two of us dispersed with the fog. It is the season of cold foods.


VIII

And thirst, my memory is of thirst, I below, at the bottom, in the well, I drank, I remember.


IX

To fall like a wounded animal in the place that was to be one of revelations.


X

As though it were nothing. Nothing at all. Mouth sewn shut. Eyelids sewn shut. I forgot.

Inside, the wind. Everything closed and the wind inside.


XI

To the black sun of silence the words turned golden.


XII

But silence is certain. That is why I write. I am alone and I write. No, I am not alone.

There is someone here, trembling.


XIII

Even if I say sun and moon and star I mean things that happen to me. And what did I desire?

I desired a perfect silence.

That is why I speak.


XIV

Night has the shape of a wolf's cry.


XV

Delight of losing oneself in the image intuited. I rose from my corpse, I went in search of who I am.

Pilgrim of myself, I have gone toward the one who sleeps in a country of wind.


XVI

My endless fall into my endless fall where no one awaited me, for when I looked to see who awaited me I saw nothing but myself.


XVII

Something was falling in the silence. My last word was I, but I meant the luminous dawn.


XVIII

Yellow flowers constellate a circle of blue earth. The water trembles, full of wind.


XIX

Dazzlement of day, yellow birds in the morning. One hand unties darkness, one hand drags

the hair of a drowned woman who never stops passing through the mirror. I must return to the memory of the body,

I must return to my grieving bones, I must understand what my voice says.

translation.title: Paths of the Mirror
translation.editorial_note: The numbered prose-poem sequence is preserved; source display wraps within sections are joined where needed so the English keeps each complete fragment together.
